title: When lifting virtualized code changes the question
summary: IDontCode and naci's 2026 Themida article describes guided symbolic evaluation as an alternative to matching individual virtual-machine handlers. For anti-cheat research, its main lesson is that recovered code must preserve original semantics and retain explicit uncertainty about protected binaries.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: A recovered native-looking function is a research artifact whose behavioral fidelity matters more than its appearance.
The article favors generic intermediate-representation optimizations over fragile per-handler fingerprints while retaining VM-specific control-flow handling.
This is research on obfuscation, not a report that a named anti-cheat was bypassed.
